newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-BYSHOVETS LEAVES KOREA TO COACH ST PETERSBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BYSHOVETS LEAVES KOREA TO COACH ST PETERSBURG.

text.p: Russian premier league side Zenit St Petersburg named former Soviet Union coach Anatoly Byshovets as their head trainer on Friday.

Byshovets was working as the South Korean national coach. Zenit executive director Viktor Sidorov told Reuters the board favoured Byshovets, who also played for the Soviet Union, over ex-Russia manager Pavel Sadyrin, who had hoped to be reinstated after his contract at Zenit ran out two weeks ago.

Players and fans of the St Petersburg side, who finished the season this month in 10th place, had campaigned for the board to overturn a decision to sack Sadyrin, who coached Russia to the 1994 World Cup finals.

Local politicians, including the governor of Russia's second city, joined the protests, pointing out that in two years the 54-year-old Sadyrin had won promotion last year and ensured a respectable finish in the premiership this year.

The directors were disappointed, however, that a home defeat to champions Spartak Moscow on the final day of the season deprived Zenit of a large cash bonus which the local council had offered as an incentive if the side finished in the top eight.

Sidorov said Byshovets, 50, who led the Soviet side to Olympic gold in the 1988 Seoul Olympics and who is credited with fashioning the South Koreans into a useful international side, agreed with the board's policy of developing local talent.
In his playing days, Byshovets was a top-scoring striker with Dynamo Kiev and the Soviet national side.
In an open letter to disgruntled fans, the board criticised Sadyrin for wanting to buy in stars for next season.
"We believe most Peterburgers support us not because they are fans of titles or bought-in prestige but of our city," they said. "Byshovets completely shares these views."
